key_insight: Interferometric reconstruction of four-wave-mixing fields from 2D perovskite (PEA)2PbI4 shows that quantum communication security depends strongly on coherence time, population time, and wavelength, with population-time control giving the best secret-bit performance.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to screen nonlinear optical materials for quantum-secure light sources using measurable spectroscopic parameters instead of requiring full photon-number-resolved detection.
method: Compute effective density matrices, Holevo bound, and secret-bits-per-pulse
evidence_signal: Across excitonic resonances, including coherence-time as a degree of freedom lowers the Holevo bound by about 2.6–5.8%, and the study maps secret-bit rates versus coherence time, population time, and detection wavelength.
watch_item: Results are model-dependent and derived from effective single-photon polarization states, so practical deployment will still require validation under real detector noise, loss, and source fluctuations.
paper_title: Security Metrics for Nonlinear Optical Light Sources from Interferometric Field Reconstruction
